title: Better Policies, Worse Verifier Audits

paper.title: Better Policies, Worse Verifier Audits
paper.abstract:
Abstract Verifier stacks increasingly sit inside post-training and test-time compute loops. We study a
specific control loop: a component verifier is evaluated on fresh policy outputs against the full success label and refreshed when that aggregate score falls. For a conjunctive target y = F ∧ M y=F\wedge M , its on-policy AUC is ( 1 − q ) ​ A own + q ​ A cross (1-q)A_{\rm own}+qA_{\rm cross} , where q = Pr ⁡ [ F = 1 ∣ y = 0 ] q=\Pr[F=1\mid y=0] . As the policy masters F F , q q can rise toward one, removing weight from F F -failures and rewarding information about M M . We call this on-policy audit collapse .
We derive a sharp identified set, a complete-erasure threshold, and the exact point at which the
audit can prefer a worse component verifier; its population optimum is the full-outcome predictor,
not the component oracle. An exact oracle exhibits the collapse, a natural multi-label text control
shows inversion can select a head with lower canonical F F -AUC at the observed failure mixture,
and a prediction-registered ECG study shows that acting on the audit can reduce off-policy F F -AUC,
transfer the damage to an unseen generator, and increase downstream constraint violations. Preserving
own-failure support prevents the damage. Matching label-complexity bounds and a controlled-mixture
audit give the corresponding repair: audit the component on its own failures, and keep those failures
in the refresh distribution.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Verifier stacks increasingly sit inside the optimization loop. Post-training systems combine outcome, process, rubric and constraint signals, while test-time compute uses verifier scores to search, rank and select candidates ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ; Lightman et al., 2024 ; Brown et al., 2024 ; Snell et al., 2025 ; Mahmoud et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2023 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ; Moskovitz et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2026 ; Bai et al., 2026 ) . A natural but unsafe control loop is to monitor a component verifier on fresh policy samples against the full task outcome; if that aggregate score drops, collect new on-policy data and refresh the verifier. Policy-interaction data are in fact used to refine reward models and iterative RLHF pipelines repeatedly update preference models on fresh policy data ( Bai et al., 2022 ; Sun et al., 2025 ) . This paper shows that this loop can become systematically wrong because the policy improved . Let success require y = F ∧ M y=F\wedge M and let s F s_{F} be a verifier intended to score F F . Among failures, some violate F F and others already satisfy F F but fail only M M . Pairwise additivity of AUC gives AUC ⁡ ( s F ; y ) = ( 1 − q ) ​ A own + q ​ A cross , q = Pr ⁡ [ F = 1 ∣ y = 0 ] . \operatorname{AUC}(s_{F};y)=(1-q)A_{\rm own}+qA_{\rm cross},\qquad q=\Pr[F=1\mid y=0]. (1) Here A own A_{\rm own} is the audit’s own-failure separability : target successes versus F F -failures. It is not, in general, identical to canonical F F -AUC; Section 2 separates the two estimands explicitly. A cross A_{\rm cross} compares successes with failures that already satisfy F F ; an exact F F -oracle has A cross = 1 / 2 A_{\rm cross}=1/2 by construction. When optimization increases satisfaction of F F faster than the remaining conjunct—in particular as F F saturates while M M remains imperfect— q q rises. Consequently, the standard aggregate monitor progressively removes weight from the verifier’s own failure mode and places it on information about the other conjunct. The paradox is therefore directional: the more completely the policy masters a component, the less the usual on-policy audit measures that component. We call this on-policy audit collapse : optimization removes the very failure mode needed to evaluate the module that learned it. This creates a concrete failure chain. First, the monitor loses identification: a falling AUC need not imply a worse component verifier. Second, it can become actively anti-aligned with the audit’s intended subproblem: at a calculable q ∗ q^{\ast} it prefers a head with worse A own A_{\rm own} because that head leaks information about M M ; in our text and engine controls this can also select a head with worse canonical F F -AUC. Third, the usual response to a bad monitor—on-policy refresh—can remove component competence. Once optimization has depleted F F -failures, refresh data alone no longer identify the boundary the component verifier must retain; outcome labels can actively entangle it, while even correct F F labels cannot reconstruct failures absent from support. The result can look benign on the monitored distribution while becoming worse exactly on the off-support failures a constraint checker must catch after a generator, prompt distribution, or policy shift. policy learns F F F F -failures vanish q ↑ q\!\uparrow audit changes meaning cross-signal wins refresh can forget F F Viewed as a learning system, this is a control-plane failure: optimizing the policy changes the data used to decide whether its verifier should be replaced or refreshed.

sections.heading: When does the failure apply?
sections.text: The central result requires three ingredients: a head intended for component F F , an on-policy audit against the full outcome y y rather than a component-specific label, and use of that audit to compare, early-stop or trigger refreshes. If trusted F F labels are available and the component is audited directly (preferably on a reference distribution that preserves F F -failures), the collapse in Eq. 1 is avoided. Our claim is therefore about this specific but natural interface, not about every verifier evaluation protocol.

sections.heading: Why this interface is current.
sections.text: Its ingredients already coexist in modern post-training systems. Rubric RL independently scores prompt-specific criteria and aggregates them into a scalar on-policy reward ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ; Mahmoud et al., 2026 ) ; policy-aware rubric work reports that substantial criterion mass is already saturated or dead under current policies ( Tyagi et al., 2026 ) ; and fresh policy-interaction data are used to refine reward models or preference models ( Sun et al., 2025 ; Bai et al., 2022 ) . We do not claim that these systems implement our exact audit-trigger-refresh controller end to end. They establish that criterion-level verifiers, policy-induced saturation, scalar aggregation and on-policy refinement are contemporary ingredients; Appendix AD.3 maps the interfaces explicitly. Our experiments are organized to test this chain rather than to accumulate unrelated benchmarks. The engine domain gives an exact component oracle, allowing us to separate real verifier failure from a case-mix artifact. GSM8K supplies a familiar language-domain negative control for ranking inversion. A natural multi-label GoEmotions stress test uses separately annotated semantic criteria to test audit collapse, inversion and refresh under support depletion; a constructed AG News control is reported in the appendix. ECG then stresses the operational consequence on a frozen external benchmark with three generator families, subject-held-out splits, two refresh model classes, downstream best-of- 16 16 selection, and a precommitted set of predictions. Across these settings the observations line up with the mechanism: exact-oracle AUC collapses, the analytic inversion threshold predicts where inversion does and does not occur, optimization removes own-failure support, outcome refresh damages off-policy canonical F F -AUC and downstream constraints in every paired split, and deliberately restoring failure support prevents the damage.

sections.heading: Contributions.
sections.text: (1) On-policy audit collapse. We derive the mixture law, a sharp identified set, and the complete-erasure threshold q ≥ max ⁡ ( A , 1 − A ) q\geq\max(A,1-A) (Section 4 ). (2) Audit inversion. We give the threshold q ∗ q^{\ast} at which cross-component signal overtakes own-failure separability and show that the aggregate audit’s population maximizer is the full-outcome predictor, not the component oracle (Proposition 2 ). (3) The refresh trap. A controlled semantic-language stress test and a prediction-registered ECG study separate label mismatch from support mismatch and connect refresh to downstream harm (Section 5 ). (4) Support-preserving repair. We give matching passive label-complexity bounds and a designed two-mixture audit whose error does not depend on the deployed policy’s saturation (Section 6 ). Downstream selection/training-interface results are deliberately kept as a boundary analysis in the appendix.

sections.heading: 2 Mechanism-first evaluation
sections.text: We test the chain implied by Eq. 1 , not a collection of interchangeable benchmarks. Engine supplies an exact oracle and matched pools for the inversion threshold; GSM8K is a language-domain negative control where inversion should not occur; GoEmotions supplies two separately annotated semantic criteria; and ECG is the frozen operational stress test with three generator families, subject-held-out evaluation, two refresh model classes and a downstream gate. Protocols and domain-specific details are in the appendices. In every domain y = F ∧ M y=F\wedge M . We keep two component estimands distinct. The theory isolates own-failure separability A own = AUC ( s F ; F = 1 , M = 1 vs F = 0 ) A_{\rm own}=\operatorname{AUC}(s_{F};F{=}1,M{=}1\text{ vs }F{=}0) , because these are exactly the outcome-audit pairs whose negative is an F F -failure. Canonical component quality is instead A F = AUC ( s F ; F = 1 vs F = 0 ) A_{F}=\operatorname{AUC}(s_{F};F{=}1\text{ vs }F{=}0) . They need not agree: if ρ = Pr ⁡ [ M = 1 ∣ F = 1 ] \rho=\Pr[M=1\mid F=1] and A aux = AUC ( s F ; F = 1 , M = 0 vs F = 0 ) A_{\rm aux}=\operatorname{AUC}(s_{F};F{=}1,M{=}0\text{ vs }F{=}0) , then A F = ρ ​ A own + ( 1 − ρ ) ​ A aux . A_{F}=\rho A_{\rm own}+(1-\rho)A_{\rm aux}. (2) Equation 2 is just the law of total probability over M M within the canonical positive class F = 1 F=1 ; no independence assumption is used. Propositions 1 – 2 characterize what the outcome audit identifies and rewards about A own A_{\rm own} ; whenever we claim actual component degradation we report A F A_{F} separately. sections.heading: The exact-oracle control rules out that interpretation.
sections.text: The component itself remains available. Two unused engine critics with different seeds show the same on-policy collapse ( 0.45 0.45 – 0.58 0.58 ) while their mass heads stay at 0.96 0.96 – 0.98 0.98 ; the feasibility head retains own-property AUC 0.940 0.940 – 0.991 0.991 on matched DPO pools, and the GSM8K format head retains 0.995 0.995 accuracy against unboxed failures. More strongly, the next section shows that an exact component oracle exhibits the same aggregate symptom. Thus the collapse cannot, by itself, identify component degradation. It is the empirical signature predicted by a changing failure mixture.

sections.heading: Optimization drives audits into this regime.
sections.text: On the post-DPO ECG test pools, scored by the same frozen critic, the within-pool own-failure bin of the deployability head is empty in every evaluable pool of the four evaluable Llama gate/inference runs and in 64 64 – 72 % 72\% of evaluable pools of the six Phi gate/inference runs, up from 13 % 13\% and 36 % 36\% at base. There no passive audit recovers A own A_{\rm own} from the deployed mixture (Section 6 ), and the on-policy refresh data no longer identify how the head should rank the missing own-failure mode. The next section tests what happens when a refresh procedure acts on that depleted support.

sections.heading: 5 The refresh trap: acting on audit collapse
sections.text: Proposition 2 describes what the aggregate audit prefers. Deployment makes the problem operational: a low monitor value can trigger collection of fresh policy samples and a verifier refresh. The mixture law predicts two distinct hazards. Label mismatch: if a component verifier is refreshed against the full outcome y y , optimization explicitly moves it toward the audit’s preferred entangled predictor. Support mismatch: even with the correct component labels F F , a saturated policy may provide almost no F F -failures, so the refresh data contain little or no information about the decision boundary the verifier must retain. The second hazard means the problem is not fixed simply by choosing the “right” label.

sections.heading: Natural multi-label semantic stress test.
sections.text: On GoEmotions ( Demszky et al., 2020 ) , keep F F as absence of annoyance and use a post-hoc, transparently reported high- q q positive control with M M = absence of gratitude . At the naturally observed q = .522 q=.522 , the component specialist has canonical F F -AUC .679 .679 but an aggregate audit of only .442 .442 . The deliberately entangled score z ⁡ ( s F ) + z ⁡ ( s M ) z(s_{F})+z(s_{M}) has substantially worse canonical F F -AUC ( .570 .570 ) yet the aggregate audit prefers it ( .681 .681 ; bootstrap 95% difference [ .210 , .270 ] [.210,.270] ), with predicted crossing q ∗ = .126 q^{*}=.126 . Sweeping leakage strength s λ = z ⁡ ( s F ) + λ ​ z ​ ( s M ) s_{\lambda}=z(s_{F})+\lambda z(s_{M}) produces the same quantitative tradeoff: as canonical F F -AUC falls from .668 .668 to .483 .483 , the observed aggregate audit rises from .470 .470 to .725 .725 . Support depletion is equally directional. With correct F F labels, canonical F F -AUC is .545 .545 when only eight own failures remain; adding 80 random development examples barely changes it ( .550 .550 ), whereas adding 80 targeted own failures raises it to .606 .606 (full support .679 .679 ). The pair choice, leakage sweep, random-vs-targeted replay and the original near-boundary disapproval control are all post hoc and reported in full in Appendix AD.6 ; AG News supplies an independent constructed replication (Appendix AD.7 ). Immediately before this study, the post-DPO ECG pools already exhibit the predicted support shift: the own-failure bin of the deployability head is empty in every evaluable pool of the four Llama gate/inference runs and in 64 64 – 72 % 72\% of evaluable pools of the six Phi runs, versus 13 % 13\% and 36 % 36\% at base. We therefore test not merely whether the monitor changes, but whether acting on it causes measurable off-policy and downstream harm.

sections.heading: Protocol: held-out subjects, two refresh classes, and an unseen generator.
sections.text: We use the frozen ECG pools, where F F is a hard deployment constraint: a valid pipeline within latency, cycle and RAM budgets. For Llama and Phi, a specialist S S is trained on the base-policy train pool with F F labels, in two head classes: an MLP with the frozen critic’s architecture and gradient-boosted trees. Refresh data are post-DPO test pools from one half of test subjects; every reported refresh metric is evaluated on the complementary subject half over 10 10 random subject splits. R y R_{y} refreshes with outcome labels, R F R_{F} with component labels, and R mix R_{\rm mix} with component labels plus an equal number of re-injected base-policy candidates. We evaluate four levels of evidence: the on-policy monitor, off-policy F F -AUC on the source generator, transfer F F -AUC on unseen Gemma outputs, and a best-of- 16 16 gated consumer. Six predictions were hashed before the run (Appendix AD ); an exploratory pilot using a different head procedure and split seed had informed P1–P3, while P4–P6 were untested. The four family × \times head-class configurations are the primary experimental settings; the 10 overlapping subject splits within each setting are robustness resamples, so counts such as 40 / 40 40/40 below report sign consistency rather than 40 independent replications. sections.heading: Result 1: the monitor selects the wrong representation.
sections.text: P1 held in all four family × \times class settings. Among heads trained from the same base data with label mixture ( 1 − λ ) ​ F + λ ​ y (1-\lambda)F+\lambda y , the pure component head ( λ = 0 \lambda=0 ) had the lowest on-policy aggregate AUC, despite F F -AUC 1.000 1.000 . This is the empirical analogue of Proposition 2 : adding outcome information improves the audit score while moving the representation away from a pure component verifier.

sections.heading: Result 2: outcome refresh causes systematic off-policy forgetting.
sections.text: P3 and P5 held. Relative to the deployed specialist, R y R_{y} lowered source-generator off-policy F F -AUC with the same sign in every held-out-subject split across both families and both head classes ( 40 / 40 40/40 paired evaluations; sign robustness, not independent replications): by 0.09 0.09 – 0.12 0.12 for MLPs and 0.43 0.43 – 0.48 0.48 for GBMs. The effect is not confined to the refresh generator: on unseen Gemma it drops 0.29 0.29 – 0.51 0.51 . By contrast, the monitor itself is not a consistent indicator of this damage: its mean change is positive in two settings and negative in two, and the preregistered P2 prediction that Phi’s monitor would improve by at least 0.05 0.05 in both classes failed ( + 0.042 +0.042 , − 0.012 -0.012 ). The intervention can therefore destroy the component without producing a reliable improvement even in the statistic that motivated it.

sections.heading: Result 3: the forgotten component changes downstream decisions.
sections.text: P6 held. Using R y R_{y} as the feasibility gate of a best-of- 16 16 selector increases constraint violations with the same sign in every held-out-subject split across both families and both head classes ( 40 / 40 40/40 paired evaluations; sign robustness, not independent replications), by + 0.011 +0.011 to + 0.055 +0.055 above the unavoidable floor, and lowers Answer@16 by 0.02 0.02 – 0.06 0.06 . This closes the loop from an apparently bad audit to an operationally worse consumer: the effect is not only a metric disagreement.

sections.heading: Result 4: correct labels are insufficient; restored support is sufficient here.
sections.text: R F R_{F} isolates support mismatch from label mismatch. It still loses 0.235 0.235 source-generator F F -AUC in the Llama-GBM setting and admits more violations, despite being refreshed with the correct component labels. In contrast, P4 held for R mix R_{\rm mix} : re-injecting base-policy candidates while keeping component labels preserves F F -AUC at 1.000 1.000 in every source setting, keeps unseen-generator AUC at 0.998 0.998 – 1.000 1.000 , and returns the gate metrics to the deployed specialist. The difference between R F R_{F} and R mix R_{\rm mix} is support, not supervision.

sections.heading: Closed-loop counterfactual.
sections.text: Composing the frozen trigger signal with the already-trained refresh heads closes the loop without new training. Refreshing with R y R_{y} whenever aggregate audit AUC falls by at least .05 .05 from base triggers all four primary settings even though each deployed specialist retains F F -AUC 1.000 1.000 ; the resulting mean F F -AUC/violation/Answer@16 changes from 1.000 / .148 / .530 1.000/.148/.530 to .719 / .179 / .491 .719/.179/.491 . Thresholds .10 .10 – .25 .25 trigger fewer settings but remain worse than no refresh on all three outcomes; a reference-distribution F F -specific trigger fires in none. The full trigger–harm curve is shown in Appendix AD.5 .

sections.heading: Empirical conclusion.
sections.text: Across the study, five of six registered predictions held. More importantly, the evidence follows the mechanism at four levels: the audit rewards entanglement, optimization removes own-failure support, refresh causes held-out and cross-generator component forgetting, and that forgetting raises downstream violations. The failed prediction is informative rather than cosmetic: the monitored AUC is not reliably repaired by refresh, strengthening the narrower conclusion that it is an unsuitable control signal. The successful rescue identifies the actionable fix used in the next section: preserve or deliberately reconstruct the component’s own failure distribution.

sections.heading: When can the audit recover component behavior?
sections.text: Three routes exist: condition directly on semantic failure bins when they have support; impose an externally justified restriction A cross ∈ [ ℓ , u ] A_{\rm cross}\in[\ell,u] , which for q < 1 q<1 gives A own ∈ [ max ⁡ ( 0 , A − q ​ u 1 − q ) , min ⁡ ( 1 , A − q ​ ℓ 1 − q ) ] ; A_{\rm own}\in\left[\max\!\left(0,\tfrac{A-qu}{1-q}\right),\min\!\left(1,\tfrac{A-q\ell}{1-q}\right)\right]; (6) or vary the failure mixture with bin-conditional distributions fixed, which by Proposition 1 reduces recovery to the rank of the mixture matrix and also restores support lost to saturation (Appendix P ). This is a designed reweighting/resampling operation, not a license to treat arbitrary policy checkpoints as mixture rows: if either bin-conditional score distribution changes, naive two-row inversion is biased. Appendix S gives the explicit drift term and an empirical boundary case where A own A_{\rm own} shifts from .965 .965 to .821 .821 out of distribution and the transported forecast misses by .101 .101 . Across two policies, the AUC change splits exactly into a mixture-shift term and conditional-ordering drift, so both mechanisms can coexist (Eq. 7 , Appendix AC ).

sections.heading: 7 Scope: what the results do and do not establish
sections.text: The AUC symptom does not identify its cause: an exact oracle collapses and an unbounded autoencoder genuinely exploits the critic (feasibility 0.9999 0.9999 predicted, 1.8 % 1.8\% actual; Appendix F ); this is not a claim that in-bounds exploitation is absent. Proposition 2 is exact, but its engine and GSM8K checks reuse published quantities and are post-hoc. The GoEmotions study is a post-hoc natural multi-label text stress test with a small bag-of-words verifier; the AG News experiment is a more constructed control with 24 deterministic robustness splits rather than independent replications. Together they establish that the mechanism is not specific to engineered numeric features, not that our refresh effect has been measured with an LLM-scale semantic verifier. Contemporary rubric-RL work independently shows criterion-level saturation and scalar aggregation at LLM scale ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ; Tyagi et al., 2026 ) ; we use that literature only to establish interface relevance, not as validation of our inversion or refresh claims. The ECG refresh study is CPU-only and uses one benchmark whose component is a deterministic resource constraint, two head classes and ten subject splits; we did not refresh an LLM-scale verifier, did not study online RL with a refreshed verifier, and our prediction that refresh repairs the monitor failed. Engine and GSM8K policies are Qwen2.5, the strongest training result is offline DPO with three seeds, and ECG training is informative in one family. The audit requires trusted component labels (proxy bins change the estimand); the engine oracle is simplified, and ECG is a signal-processing benchmark, not a clinical validation.

sections.heading: 8 Related work
sections.text: Modern post-training makes the component/aggregate interface concrete. Rubric RL scores prompt-specific criteria separately and then aggregates them into scalar on-policy rewards ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ; Mahmoud et al., 2026 ) ; policy-aware rubric work further shows that criterion informativeness changes with the policy because many criteria become saturated or dead ( Tyagi et al., 2026 ) . Fresh policy interactions are also used to refine reward or preference models ( Sun et al., 2025 ; Bai et al., 2022 ) . Two adjacent loop failures are especially relevant: on-policy optimization against one verifier can remove behaviors needed for later objectives ( Wei et al., 2026 ) , and a verifier useful on one task can regress a learner after task shift ( Lin, 2026 ) . We instead study the audit interface : full-outcome AUC can stop identifying one component, prefer an entangled verifier, and induce a harmful refresh even when the component verifier was initially correct. The statistical ingredients are classical. ROC behavior depends on case mix ( Sadatsafavi et al., 2022 ) ; partial identification and trimming bounds describe incomplete observables ( Manski, 2003 ; Tamer, 2010 ; Horowitz and Manski, 1995 ) ; deliberately varying mixture weights is a linear special case of finite-mixture identification ( Henry et al., 2014 ) ; the within/cross split parallels xAUC ( Kallus and Zhou, 2019 ) ; and the population AUC maximizer is the classical optimal ranker ( Clémençon et al., 2008 ) . We do not claim these ingredients as new. The new consequence is their combination under policy-induced semantic failure mixtures: complete loss of component identification, a calculable verifier-ranking inversion, and an audit-driven maintenance failure.

sections.heading: AI use statement
sections.text: Generative AI was used to improve the clarity and presentation of manuscript claims, assist with software implementation and debugging, and provide critical feedback on claims and arguments during manuscript development. AI-generated suggestions were treated as editorial and technical assistance rather than as evidence or independent validation. The authors are fully responsible for the final claims, proofs, code, citations, analyses, and submission.

sections.heading: Ethics statement
sections.text: The engine evaluations concern a simplified geometry, mass and printability model, not safety certification or fabrication validation; propulsion design can have dual-use implications. The ECG study uses public, de-identified PhysioNet recordings (MIT-BIH Arrhythmia and Noise Stress Test databases) under their published terms; it is a signal-processing deployment benchmark, not a diagnostic or clinical validation, and its outputs should not be used for patient care.

sections.heading: Reproducibility statement
sections.text: The supplement contains the exact anonymous source snapshot, the CPU-only GoEmotions and AG News semantic stress-test scripts with frozen JSON summaries, and the frozen controller threshold analysis used in the final revision. The original large engine/ECG/GSM8K candidate pools and model checkpoints are not bundled in this lightweight artifact; their protocols, registered predictions, assumptions and reported frozen summaries are documented in the appendix. Thus the supplement supports an exact paper rebuild and independent reruns of the public-data semantic controls, but not an end-to-end regeneration of every large system experiment from raw candidates. See Appendices G , AD.6 , AD.7 , I and K .

sections.heading: Appendix roadmap
sections.text: The appendix is intentionally evidence-first. Appendices A–AD contain the oracle definitions, core audit-collapse controls, identification proofs, transfer checks, preregistration material and the refresh/semantic experiments that support the main claim. Appendices AE–AF are optional boundary analyses of downstream selection and DPO interfaces; they are not needed for Propositions 1–3 or the refresh-trap conclusion. Bundled scripts and frozen summaries are indexed in the supplement README; appendix-only workspace paths are provenance labels and do not imply that the corresponding large artifacts are packaged.

sections.heading: Appendix A The engine oracle
sections.text: The solver decodes a design vector to a multi-zone body, computes its mass by integration, evaluates printability (overhang, minimum ligament and wall, DfAM flags) and envelope fit, and returns feasible as their conjunction, in 7.9 7.9 ms; the 200 000 200\,000 -row reference sample took 72 72 s. Its thermochemistry is checked against NASA CEA through rocketcea , independent of the project’s own Cantera path: across 28 28 operating points the maximum error is 0.25 % 0.25\% on chamber temperature and 1.7 % 1.7\% on characteristic velocity. The flow solver is grid-convergent on the Sod problem ( L 1 L_{1} error 0.0079 → 0.0042 → 0.0024 0.0079\to 0.0042\to 0.0024 at 100 / 200 / 400 100/200/400 cells) and reproduces the oblique-shock relation to 1.2 ∘ 1.2^{\circ} . Those checks cover the flow path, which is sized from the requirement and not the generator’s to choose. The on-target criterion is two-sided because under a one-sided one 86.4 % 86.4\% of on-target draws in the reference sample satisfy it by being small rather than by meeting the budget.

sections.heading: Appendix B The identity for the mass head
sections.text: With the roles swapped, the mass head’s score against y = F ∧ M y=F\wedge M decomposes as ( 1 − q ) AUC ( s M ; y = 1 vs F = 0 ) + q AUC ( s M ; y = 1 vs F = 1 , M = 0 ) (1-q)\,\mathrm{AUC}(s_{M};y{=}1\text{ vs }F{=}0)+q\,\mathrm{AUC}(s_{M};y{=}1\text{ vs }F{=}1,M{=}0) . The second term is the head’s own sub-problem and is 0.96 0.96 – 0.99 0.99 on every arm; the first is 0.84 0.84 – 0.95 0.95 , since infeasible designs are also, on average, further from the budget. sections.heading: Residual spread is not uniformly noise.
sections.text: We permute feasibility logits within each requirement’s predicted passing set, preserving the set and mass scores, and re-evaluate the raw sum (100 permutations). On gated 7B pools mean raw answer falls from 0.237 0.237 to 0.209 0.209 : residual ordering retains useful signal. This does not make the raw sum competitive with two-stage selection, but it precludes treating all residual feasibility variation as irrelevant noise. Permutation is a conditional score ablation, not an intervention on training.

sections.heading: Parsing and the second-round lineage.
sections.text: Relative to the single parent policy, sum-ranked children lose supply even on requirements where both parent and child pools are fully parsed: differences − 0.141 -0.141 , − 0.110 -0.110 , − 0.061 -0.061 on 915 915 , 762 762 , 685 685 requirements. Gated children improve supply on the corresponding subsets by 0.050 0.050 , 0.103 0.103 , 0.218 0.218 . This shows that format breakage alone cannot account for all observed loss; the subsets are post-hoc and selected, so this is not a causal correction for parsing. Within-requirement coordinate spread is reported in the main text conditional on at least two successful samples.

sections.heading: Top-1 failures and sampling budget.
sections.text: The analysis artifact includes nested K = 1 , 2 , 4 , 8 , 16 K=1,2,4,8,16 answer curves, failures split into unparsed, infeasible parsed, and feasible mass misses, and the fraction of requirements with a solution that the selector misses. These directly measure the top of the ranking, which AUC alone does not determine. For matched sum DPO at 1.5B, the raw sum misses an available solution on 0.446 0.446 – 0.482 0.482 of requirements, compared with 0.035 0.035 – 0.048 0.048 under two-stage selection.

sections.heading: Registered predictions and outcomes.
sections.text: Before any result was read ( PREREG_TUNED_SUM_THEORY_2026-09-18.md ) we registered, from the aggregation argument of § AE , that the tuned sum and the log-probability form would each land within 0.04 0.04 of the gate’s composed answer and 0.05 0.05 of its per-draw rate and supply (T1, T2), that mass-only would stay below 0.70 0.70 composed with the falsifier “within 0.03 0.03 of the gate” (T3), that every new arm would beat the unit sum (T4), and that q > 0.9 q>0.9 and A own > 0.9 A_{\rm own}>0.9 on every tuned-sum and log-prob arm (T5). T3 held on every seed and the falsifier did not fire. T1, T2 and T4 missed: the tuned sum is 0.187 0.187 below the gate, the log-probability form 0.082 0.082 below, and the tuned sum and mass-only fall below the unit sum on composed answer. T5 missed on q q for the tuned sum ( 0.57 0.57 – 0.63 0.63 ) with A own > 0.92 A_{\rm own}>0.92 everywhere. The prediction that failed was the extrapolation of a selection-side argument to pair construction; the selection-side part held (the validation-selected weight lies in the registered band [ 0.001 , 0.005 ] [0.001,0.005] ).

sections.heading: Why the tuned weight is the wrong training weight.
sections.text: Figure 8 sweeps w w over the train pool. Among parsed train candidates the logit’s spread ( 9.96 9.96 ) is ten times the mass term’s ( 0.97 0.97 ), so the pair contrast in feasibility, Δ ​ F \Delta F , falls monotonically as w w shrinks while the mass contrast Δ ​ M \Delta M rises: ( 0.64 , 0.11 ) (0.64,0.11) at w = 1 w=1 , ( 0.13 , 0.82 ) (0.13,0.82) at 0.005 0.005 , ( 0.03 , 0.84 ) (0.03,0.84) at 0 0 . The gate sits at ( 0.48 , 0.63 ) (0.48,0.63) . The scalar curve passes close to that point near w ≈ 0.1 w\approx 0.1 ( ( 0.48 , 0.52 ) (0.48,0.52) ), a weight 20 × 20\times the validation-selected one and one the selection criterion ranks fifth from the bottom of thirteen; we had registered that no weight would come within 0.85 0.85 of the gate on both contrasts, and the sweep refutes that ( 0.91 0.91 at w = 0.075 w=0.075 ). The chosen sets of w = 0.1 w=0.1 and of the gate overlap 65 % 65\% , the full pairs 15 % 15\% : the gate’s rejected candidates are the infeasible ones with the worst mass term, while a scalar score rejects by whichever term dominates at that weight.

The rule returned contrast suffices : per draw 0.312 ± 0.021 0.312\pm 0.021 , feasible 0.867 0.867 , supply 0.821 ± 0.017 0.821\pm 0.017 , composed 0.770 ± 0.023 0.770\pm 0.023 , mass gain 0.98 ± 0.02 0.98\pm 0.02 , q q 0.961 0.961 , A own A_{\rm own} 0.927 0.927 (Table 15 ); the paired gate-minus-sum differences are − 0.001 -0.001 [ − 0.015 , 0.012 ] [-0.015,0.012] per draw, − 0.014 -0.014 [ − 0.031 , 0.003 ] [-0.031,0.003] supply, − 0.012 -0.012 [ − 0.030 , 0.006 ] [-0.030,0.006] composed and − 0.020 -0.020 [ − 0.039 , − 0.001 ] [-0.039,-0.001] under the log-probability selector. Every registered point value missed, all in the same direction: we had expected a partial recovery (feasible 0.79 0.79 , per draw 0.27 0.27 , composed 0.70 0.70 , gain 0.80 0.80 , envelope ρ < 0.45 \rho<0.45 ) and the policy reached the gate on every count and installed envelope conditioning as well ( 0.69 ± 0.06 0.69\pm 0.06 ), which no other rule does together with unit budget tracking. The 0.72 0.72 plateau of the three mis-weighted scalar rules is therefore a property of their contrast, not of scalar scores, and the gate’s distinctive rejected set does not matter. The base-pool forecast of § 4 lands within 0.024 0.024 on these arms. The 7B base train pool is used below to test whether the weight-selection criterion itself transfers; a later follow-up then trains the corresponding 7B scalar arm.

sections.heading: Choosing the contrast weight without gold labels.
sections.text: The trained w = 0.1 w=0.1 arm above was selected by oracle-unit contrasts Δ ​ F \Delta F and Δ ​ M \Delta M . We subsequently pre-specified a label-free repetition using only the critic on the same train pool: Δ ​ P \Delta P is the difference in predicted feasibility probability between chosen and rejected samples, and Δ ​ M ^ \Delta\widehat{M} is the reduction in predicted absolute log-mass error. Across the weight grid, Δ ​ P \Delta P and Δ ​ F \Delta F have Spearman correlation 1.000 1.000 at 1.5B and 0.999 0.999 at 7B; Δ ​ M ^ \Delta\widehat{M} and Δ ​ M \Delta M have 0.995 0.995 and 0.999 0.999 . Matching the hard gate in critic units selects w = 0.075 w=0.075 at 1.5B and w = 0.056 w=0.056 – 0.075 0.075 at 7B, the same narrow region as the oracle-unit sweep. A further post-hoc criterion removes even the gate as a reference. For each w w , we normalise Δ ​ P \Delta P and Δ ​ M ^ \Delta\widehat{M} by their respective maxima over the sweep and maximise the smaller of the two normalised contrasts. This intrinsic maximin rule selects w = 0.075 w=0.075 at 1.5B and w = 0.056 w=0.056 at 7B; maximising their product or minimising distance to the ideal point ( 1 , 1 ) (1,1) selects exactly the same weights. This criterion by itself does not prove that the resulting policy must match a gate; the 1.5B experiment above and the later 7B follow-up below test that training claim. It answers the practical weight-selection question using critic outputs alone and is distinct from the failed label-free diagnostic in Appendix T .

sections.heading: Post-hoc split stability of the intrinsic criterion.
sections.text: As a sampling-sensitivity check, we recompute the critic-only maximin rule on the independently generated base test pools, which were not used to build the training pairs. It selects exactly the train-pool choices: w = 0.074989 w=0.074989 at 1.5B and w = 0.056234 w=0.056234 at 7B. In 500 requirement-bootstrap resamples of each test pool, the 1.5B maximin choice is 0.074989 0.074989 in 499 / 500 499/500 resamples (and 0.1 0.1 once); at 7B it is 0.056234 0.056234 in 415 / 500 415/500 , 0.05 0.05 in 66 / 500 66/500 and 0.074989 0.074989 in 19 / 500 19/500 . Thus every resample at both scales stays in the same [ 0.05 , 0.10 ] [0.05,0.10] region. Product and distance-to-ideal criteria choose the same full-test-pool points. This audit is post-hoc and is evidence for split stability of the criterion, not a new policy training result.

Re-evaluating the stored pools with the common two-stage selector gives composed answer 0.565 ± 0.065 0.565\pm 0.065 , compared with 0.562 ± 0.026 0.562\pm 0.026 for the matched 7B hard gate. sections.heading: Controlled-mixture audit design.
sections.text: Suppose the bin-specific ordering vector a a is held fixed while an auditor constructs K K negative mixtures with known rows π ( k ) \pi^{(k)} . Writing Π \Pi for the resulting K × J K\times J matrix, the aggregate audits satisfy A = Π ​ a A=\Pi a . Hence a a is point-identified for every possible value iff rank ⁡ ( Π ) = J \operatorname{rank}(\Pi)=J ; otherwise a null-space direction that remains inside [ 0 , 1 ] J [0,1]^{J} is observationally equivalent. For the binary split, two audits with q 1 ≠ q 2 q_{1}\neq q_{2} give A own = q 2 ​ A 1 − q 1 ​ A 2 q 2 − q 1 , A cross = ( 1 − q 1 ) ​ A 2 − ( 1 − q 2 ) ​ A 1 q 2 − q 1 . A_{\rm own}=\frac{q_{2}A_{1}-q_{1}A_{2}}{q_{2}-q_{1}},\qquad A_{\rm cross}=\frac{(1-q_{1})A_{2}-(1-q_{2})A_{1}}{q_{2}-q_{1}}. This is a controlled-reweighting result; it does not license combining ordinary policy checkpoints whose conditional score distributions may themselves change. A useful corollary is the exact condition for complete loss of information about A own A_{\rm own} when q < 1 q<1 : its sharp interval is [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] iff 1 − q ≤ A ≤ q 1-q\leq A\leq q . All four matched engine rows in Table 2 satisfy this condition. The result is an identification statement about the aggregate statistic; it does not say that direct own-bin estimates are unreliable when their support is adequate.

sections.text: For two candidates i , j i,j scored by r w = w ​ s F + s M r_{w}=ws_{F}+s_{M} , their order can change only when w ⁡ ( s F , i − s F , j ) + ( s M , i − s M , j ) = 0 . w(s_{F,i}-s_{F,j})+(s_{M,i}-s_{M,j})=0. Thus, away from the finite set of pairwise crossing weights, every within-pool ranking is fixed. Any top- k k selector and any deterministic top-versus-bottom pair builder is consequently piecewise constant in w w . If two rules induce the same chosen–rejected multiset, the DPO loss is literally the same function of the policy parameters because the scalar score is no longer an input to DPO. sections.heading: Appendix R Perfect-conjunct and finite-pool controls
sections.text: These are post-hoc controls on existing candidates, not part of the original preregistration. The exact feasibility oracle (engine) and boxed-format regex (GSM8K) replace only the head of the corresponding conjunct for AUC measurement. A binary perfect conjunct head ties every successful candidate with every failure that satisfies that conjunct. Thus its full-target AUC is 1 − q / 2 1-q/2 , with half credit for ties. We average over requirements containing both target classes; engine candidates are parsed-only. Support is 285 285 base requirements and 658,657,593 658,657,593 for the three matched 1.5B sum-DPO seeds. Their perfect-head AUCs are 0.8326 0.8326 and 0.5187 , 0.5145 , 0.5113 0.5187,0.5145,0.5113 , respectively. GSM8K support is 474 474 at base and 431,443,439 431,443,439 after sum-DPO, with AUCs 0.9219 0.9219 and 0.5189 , 0.5210 , 0.5155 0.5189,0.5210,0.5155 . Own-task oracle correctness is exact by construction; this is not an oracle for the full conjunction. We also measure best-of- k k averaged over every uniform size- k k subset of each stored GSM8K pool of N = 64 N=64 , without replacement. For a deterministic selector order, candidate rank r ∈ { 1 , … , N } r\in\{1,\ldots,N\} is selected with probability ( N − r k − 1 ) / ( N k ) \binom{N-r}{k-1}/\binom{N}{k} ; averaging its target label with these weights gives the exact conditional answer rate. Supply is 1 − ( N − P k ) / ( N k ) 1-\binom{N-P}{k}/\binom{N}{k} , where P P is the number of successes. Ties use original candidate index. Exhaustive small-pool subset enumeration verifies the implementation. This is a finite-pool estimator, not a new scaling law or a prediction beyond N N ; related ROC-based scaling theory is in Dorner et al. (2026) . For sum-DPO, averaging training seeds, raw-sum answers at k = 4 , 16 , 64 k=4,16,64 are 0.693 , 0.680 , 0.645 0.693,0.680,0.645 , versus base 0.606 , 0.736 , 0.762 0.606,0.736,0.762 . Supplies after sum-DPO are 0.839 , 0.929 , 0.969 0.839,0.929,0.969 at those budgets. Replacing the learned format gate with the exact boxed regex and retaining the learned correctness ranker gives 0.679 0.679 at k = 16 k=16 and 0.639 0.639 at k = 64 k=64 after sum-DPO (base 0.737 , 0.758 0.737,0.758 ). This control removes format-classification error without repairing the remaining ranker. It does not establish impossibility for other correctness models or selection methods. Finally, a fixed scale grid T ∈ { 0.01 , 0.1 , 1 , 10 , 100 } T\in\{0.01,0.1,1,10,100\} applied to feasibility logits preserves every head AUC but changes raw-sum answers. Matched 1.5B sum-DPO has mean answers 0.544 , 0.312 , 0.185 , 0.162 , 0.160 0.544,0.312,0.185,0.162,0.160 , respectively. This test-set sensitivity analysis illustrates the distinction between ranking metrics and aggregation units; it is not validation-based hyperparameter tuning. Code and complete tables are in scripts/audit_perfect_head.py , scripts/audit_gsm_tails.py , and the corresponding results directories. The paired requirement-bootstrap difference (sum-DPO minus base), conditional on these fixed training seeds, is − 0.0555 -0.0555 [ − 0.0738 , − 0.0368 -0.0738,-0.0368 ] for raw-sum answers at k = 16 k=16 and − 0.1167 -0.1167 [ − 0.1500 , − 0.0833 -0.1500,-0.0833 ] at k = 64 k=64 . Exact-format-gate differences are − 0.0578 -0.0578 [ − 0.0767 , − 0.0402 -0.0767,-0.0402 ] and − 0.1193 -0.1193 [ − 0.1533 , − 0.0873 -0.1533,-0.0873 ]. These intervals quantify requirement uncertainty, not population training-seed uncertainty. Figure 9: Post-hoc controls. Right: GSM8K finite-pool subset-averaged answers; exact format gating does not repair the remaining correctness ranker. Bands show training-seed SD, not confidence intervals.

sections.heading: Appendix S Transfer forecast of on-policy AUC
sections.text: Equation 3 is exact on the pool whose terms it uses, so reconstructing an AUC there is arithmetic rather than evidence. This control asks the out-of-sample question instead. The bin terms A own A_{\rm own} and A cross A_{\rm cross} are measured on a source pool; from a target pool we read only q q and never the head’s ordering; we then predict the target’s on-policy AUC. Every arm answers the same committed test split, so requirement i i denotes the same requirement in both pools: a prediction is formed per requirement and averaged over the requirements that contain both target classes in both pools. We compare four predictors: chance ( 1 2 \tfrac{1}{2} ); persistence , the source pool’s own AUC, which is what assuming an earlier audit of the same verifier still describes the policy amounts to; the zero-parameter form ( 1 − q ) ​ A own + q / 2 (1-q)A_{\rm own}+q/2 ; and the transported form ( 1 − q ) ​ A own + q ​ A cross (1-q)A_{\rm own}+qA_{\rm cross} . Five protocols supply 57 57 source–target pairs: the 1.5B base pool to 26 26 trained 1.5B arms (matched sum and hard-gate DPO, the earlier DPO arms, the five IPO/DPO mitigation arms, both GRPO rewards and the second round), the 7B base pool to 9 9 trained 7B arms, the 1.5B base pool to those same 9 9 7B arms, the 1.5B base pool to 7 7 cVAE-family pools scored by the same critic, and the GSM8K base pool to its 6 6 trained arms. Measured arm AUC spans 0.408 0.408 to 0.937 0.937 .

sections.heading: Why ordinary checkpoints are not a designed two-mixture audit.
sections.text: Suppose an auditor observes ( A 1 , q 1 ) (A_{1},q_{1}) and ( A 2 , q 2 ) (A_{2},q_{2}) but the conditional terms drift from ( a 1 , c 1 ) (a_{1},c_{1}) to ( a 2 , c 2 ) (a_{2},c_{2}) . If it nevertheless applies the fixed-component inversion a ^ = ( q 2 ​ A 1 − q 1 ​ A 2 ) / ( q 2 − q 1 ) \hat{a}=(q_{2}A_{1}-q_{1}A_{2})/(q_{2}-q_{1}) , then relative to the first pool a ^ − a 1 = q 1 ​ ( 1 − q 2 ) ​ ( a 1 − a 2 ) + q 1 ​ q 2 ​ ( c 1 − c 2 ) q 2 − q 1 . \hat{a}-a_{1}=\frac{q_{1}(1-q_{2})(a_{1}-a_{2})+q_{1}q_{2}(c_{1}-c_{2})}{q_{2}-q_{1}}. Thus separation in mixture weights cannot remove conditional drift; it can amplify it when | q 2 − q 1 | |q_{2}-q_{1}| is small. Proposition 3 (ii) is therefore a statement about controlled reweighting/resampling of fixed bin-conditional score distributions . The transfer experiments below ask how far that assumption approximately travels across real policy changes; they are diagnostics, not the designed-audit guarantee. sections.heading: What this does and does not establish.
sections.text: The forecast avoids re-auditing the head’s ordering on the target policy; it does not avoid target-side labels, since q q is an oracle-label statistic of the target pool. All arms existed before this control was written, so this is a post-hoc transfer protocol across stored pools, not a preregistered forward forecast of an unrun experiment. Transporting A own A_{\rm own} assumes the head’s ordering against own-conjunct failures is stable across policies; the residual errors in Table 16 bound how far that assumption travels here and do not license it for arbitrary policies, critics or tasks. Accuracy on the saturated arms is unimpressive on its own, since chance achieves it. Code: scripts/predict_auc_transfer.py ; complete per-arm tables in results/predictive_audit/ .

sections.heading: Out of distribution.
sections.text: The benchmark ships a fourth split of 500 500 requirements drawn beyond the training prior (thrust to 61.8 61.8 N against a 5 5 – 60 60 N prior, expansion ratio to 23.3 23.3 ). Fifteen stored cVAE pools answer it. Requirement indices do not correspond across splits, so this forecast is arm-level: each generator family’s mean bin terms from the test split, that family’s mean q q on the OOD split, and its OOD AUC predicted. Over the five families the zero-parameter mean absolute error is 0.0282 0.0282 , against 0.0752 0.0752 for persistence and 0.3640 0.3640 for chance, and the identity still reconstructs every OOD requirement to 10 − 9 10^{-9} . Four families land within 0.024 0.024 . The capped decoder is the exception, missing by 0.101 0.101 , and the terms say why: its own-bin ordering does not transport, falling from A own = 0.965 A_{\rm own}=0.965 on the test split to 0.821 0.821 out of distribution. That is the assumption the forecast rests on and this arm is where it breaks. The transported variant fares worse still on latent search, whose A cross A_{\rm cross} drops from 0.817 0.817 to 0.651 0.651 . sections.heading: Appendix T A label-free version of the diagnostic does not transfer
sections.text: Every measurement above needs oracle labels: q q , A own A_{\rm own} and A cross A_{\rm cross} are all label statistics. A deployed pipeline has none, so we asked whether the critic’s own scores already reveal that an additive composition is losing best-of- K K lift. Three label-free statistics were computed per arm from the two term arrays alone: the share of pools whose sum-argmax equals the saturated term’s argmax, the median within-pool SD of the saturated term over the other term’s, and the share of candidates the saturated head calls satisfied with p > 0.99 p>0.99 . They were asked to predict two oracle-measured quantities: η raw \eta_{\rm raw} , the share of attainable best-of- K K lift the additive rule captures, and the gain from switching to a gate. Leave-one-arm-out linear fits were compared against predicting the training-fold mean over 32 32 engine arms and the same 32 32 plus 7 7 GSM8K arms. On the engine arms alone the relations look usable: saturated fraction against gate gain reaches r = 0.70 r=0.70 with leave-one-out MAE 0.140 0.140 against 0.227 0.227 for the mean, and the SD ratio against η raw \eta_{\rm raw} reaches r = 0.73 r=0.73 with MAE 0.112 0.112 against 0.151 0.151 . The SD ratio’s sign is nevertheless opposite to the mechanism, because a dominant feasibility term also marks pools where feasibility genuinely discriminates. Adding GSM8K removes the effect: saturated fraction against gate gain falls to r = 0.02 r=0.02 and the SD ratio to r = − 0.14 r=-0.14 , both worse than predicting the mean ( 0.339 0.339 and 0.336 0.336 against 0.332 0.332 ). We therefore make no label-free claim. This is a negative result on three specific statistics and two targets, not a proof that no label-free diagnostic exists; a learned combination, per-requirement rather than per-arm targets, or a calibrated head might do better. Code: scripts/label_free_diagnostic.py ; full table in results/label_free_diagnostic/audit.json .

sections.heading: Appendix U Feasibility’s own sub-constraints: a case where the mix moves and the AUC does not
sections.text: The packaged oracle defines feasible as printable AND fits_envelope : no DfAM flag (overhang, minimum wall, channel-versus-ligament, minimum TPMS cell) and length ≤ \leq envelope (the radius clause 2 ​ r max ≤ 2r_{\max}\leq envelope cannot bind: 2 × 55 ​ mm < 200 ​ mm 2\times 55\,\mathrm{mm}<200\,\mathrm{mm} ). Both are consequential geometric constraints, and neither is syntactic. The main text treats feasibility as one conjunct; here we split it. The two are learned at very different rates. Printability rises from 0.396 0.396 at the 1.5B base and 0.544 0.544 at the 7B base to 0.93 0.93 – 1.00 1.00 across every matched DPO and GRPO arm; envelope fit starts at 0.808 0.808 in both bases and ends between 0.811 0.811 and 0.880 0.880 . The envelope rate is capped: for 4.9 % 4.9\% of test requirements the sized length exceeds the envelope even at the policy’s shortest setting, so no design fits. Among attainable requirements the fit rate moves from 0.85 0.85 to 0.92 0.92 under sum-ranked pairs and stays at 0.86 0.86 – 0.87 0.87 under gated pairs (Appendix W ). The composition of the head’s negative bin therefore shifts hard: writing p = Pr ⁡ [ printable ∣ not feasible ] p=\Pr[\text{printable}\mid\text{not feasible}] , the share of remaining failures that print but do not fit rises from 0.081 0.081 (1.5B base) and 0.052 0.052 (7B base) to 0.21 0.21 – 0.93 0.93 after training. Splitting the feasibility head’s negatives the same way gives AUC ⁡ ( s F , F ) = ( 1 − p ) ​ A print + p ​ A env \mathrm{AUC}(s_{F};F)=(1-p)A_{\rm print}+p\,A_{\rm env} , checked to 10 − 9 10^{-9} per requirement. Unlike the conjunctive case of the main text, the inherited term is not near chance: A env A_{\rm env} lies between 0.889 0.889 and 0.995 0.995 on every arm, and AUC ⁡ ( s F , F ) \mathrm{AUC}(s_{F};F) stays between 0.940 0.940 and 0.991 0.991 throughout. The extreme case is the 7B sum arm at seed 2, where p = 0.932 p=0.932 — almost every remaining failure is an envelope failure — and the AUC is 0.983 0.983 . This is the control the conjunctive claim needs. Negative composition moves at least as far here as it does in the main text ( q q reaching 0.98 0.98 ), in the same pools and with the same critic, and no collapse follows, because the head kept its ordering in the bin it inherited. Composition and bin quality are separately necessary; neither on its own predicts the diagnostic. The envelope-only bin is sparse on the strongest arms ( 33 33 – 201 201 supported requirements, listed per arm in the artifact), so the A env A_{\rm env} estimates there carry correspondingly wide uncertainty; the direction of the contrast does not depend on any single arm. Code: scripts/audit_feasibility_substructure.py ; per-arm table in results/subconstraint_audit/audit.json .

sections.heading: Appendix V The same critic as a training target and as a search objective
sections.text: The cVAE family lets the critic enter the generator in two different places, on one design space with one oracle. sections.heading:
The requirement-independent conjunct goes to ceiling under every rule
that contrasts it.
sections.text: Printability is 0.40 0.40 and 0.54 0.54 at the two bases and 0.93 0.93 – 1.00 1.00 on every DPO and GRPO arm whose pairs contrast feasibility; its dependence on thrust, 42 42 and 22 22 pp across terciles at the bases, falls to 0 0 – 5 5 pp on those arms. This is the conjunct whose head saturates in the main text. The two rules whose pairs barely contrast feasibility (Table 14 ) leave it short of ceiling: 0.57 ± 0.07 0.57\pm 0.07 under mass-only, whose pairs contrast it by 0.03 0.03 , and 0.80 ± 0.03 0.80\pm 0.03 under the tuned sum ( 0.13 0.13 ), with the thrust dependence of the base intact ( 35 35 – 36 36 pp). We had registered the mass-only value as 0.60 0.60 (band < 0.80 <0.80 ) before computing it.

sections.heading:
Which requirement-dependent conjunct is conditioned on is set by the
ranking rule.
sections.text: Pairs ranked by the unit-weight sum, which the saturated feasibility logit dominates, install envelope conditioning: the partial correlation of v 30 v_{30} with the envelope rises from 0.22 0.22 to 0.76 0.76 – 0.84 0.84 at 1.5B and from 0.63 0.63 to 0.91 0.91 – 0.94 0.94 at 7B, on every seed, while the mass gain reaches only 0.44 0.44 – 0.52 0.52 at 1.5B and falls from the 7B base’s 0.30 0.30 to 0.19 0.19 – 0.22 0.22 . Pairs ranked by the hard gate leave envelope conditioning where the base had it ( 0.12 0.12 – 0.16 0.16 at 1.5B; 0.48 0.48 – 0.62 0.62 at 7B) and install mass conditioning with near-unit gain: 1.03 ± 0.08 1.03\pm 0.08 at 1.5B with partial correlation 0.97 0.97 on every seed, 0.62 ± 0.06 0.62\pm 0.06 at 7B. At 1.5B the across-requirement SD of the gated policy’s mean log ⁡ m \log m is 0.66 0.66 , the SD of the log-uniform budget prior itself being 0.61 0.61 : the policy’s mass distribution has become the budget distribution. Per-draw on-target tracks mass gain, the quantity on-target requires: Spearman 0.96 0.96 over the seven trained LLM families and 0.88 0.88 with the two bases, whose printability is still far from ceiling, included. The two GRPO rewards, whose effect on supply and per-draw is small in § AF , are indistinguishable here as well ( 0.68 0.68 vs 0.60 0.60 envelope, 0.20 0.20 vs 0.21 0.21 mass). Both DPO rules still vary v 30 v_{30} within a requirement (SD 0.04 0.04 – 0.07 0.07 ); “not conditioned” means not set by the prompt, not held constant.

sections.heading:
Scalar rules that contrast mass install partial tracking; the gates
install full tracking.
sections.text: The four arms trained after this audit was written ( † \dagger in Table 21 ) test the rule-chooses-the-conjunct claim prospectively. On envelope they behave as registered: the tuned sum and mass-only leave it where the base had it ( 0.08 0.08 , 0.11 0.11 ), the log-probability form installs it like the sum ( 0.79 0.79 ), and the three-conjunct gate leaves it like the gate ( 0.11 0.11 ). On mass they do not: we registered gains of 0.95 0.95 for the tuned sum and mass-only (band [ 0.8 , 1.15 ] [0.8,1.15] ) and 0.45 0.45 for log-prob (band [ 0.3 , 0.65 ] [0.3,0.65] ), and all three land at 0.72 0.72 – 0.74 0.74 , whatever their pairs’ mass contrast ( 0.18 0.18 for log-prob, 0.81 0.81 – 0.84 0.84 for the other two); the three-conjunct gate lands at 1.06 1.06 , as registered. Across the five single-gate rules the trained printable rate follows the pairs’ feasibility contrast (Spearman 0.9 0.9 ) but mass gain does not follow the mass contrast ( 0.6 0.6 ): both gates reach unit gain with an across-requirement mass SD of 0.66 0.66 – 0.68 0.68 that matches the budget prior’s 0.61 0.61 , while these scalar rules stop at 0.44 0.44 – 0.50 0.50 . The contrast-matched sum of Appendix O settles what this means: at w = 0.1 w=0.1 a scalar score installs unit budget tracking ( 0.98 ± 0.02 0.98\pm 0.02 , mass SD 0.64 0.64 ) and envelope conditioning ( 0.69 ± 0.06 0.69\pm 0.06 ), the only rule that installs both. The plateau belonged to the wrong weights, not to scalar scores.

sections.heading: The continuous decoder takes the unconditional shortcut; search does not.
sections.text: No cVAE decoder conditions mass on the budget (gain − 0.01 -0.01 – 0.00 0.00 on all nine seeds, prior included), although the decoder is conditional by construction. Trained against the critic’s terms, the λ = 1 \lambda=1 and capped decoders satisfy the envelope by collapsing v 30 v_{30} to 0.000 ± 0.001 0.000\pm 0.001 on every seed — the shortest allowed length for every prompt — reaching fit 1.000 1.000 while printability falls to 0.00 0.00 – 0.25 0.25 . Latent search over the untrained decoder, under the same critic, attains mass gain 0.76 0.76 with partial correlation 0.99 0.99 : in the continuous representation the prompt dependence arrives through search at inference, not through the learned map. This is the same contrast as Table 20 , one level down: the critic that shapes a token policy’s conditioning through pair ranking shapes a decoder into a constant.

sections.heading: Registered predictions and misses.
sections.text: Five predictions were written before the audit ( context/docs/PLAN_CONDITIONING_2026-09-18.md ); each part is scored there. Held: sum gain below gate gain at both scales; printability flat across envelope classes; gated arms spread mass across requirements more than sum arms. Missed, in the informative direction: we predicted that trained token policies would take the decoders’ shortcut (global shrink, | ρ | < 0.15 |\rho|<0.15 ) — they condition instead, on the conjunct the rule rewards; that gated mass gain would lie in 0.30 0.30 – 0.70 0.70 — at 1.5B it is 1.03 1.03 ; that the base 7B model would not read the budget — it does, partially ( 0.30 0.30 ); and that sum arms would narrow their mass below the base’s spread — at 1.5B they widen it, because they track the budget partially. Also missed: the attainable fraction is 0.951 0.951 , not 0.90 0.90 , and printability on the 7B gated and GRPO gated arms keeps a 6 6 – 14 14 pp thrust dependence. Base and single-lineage rows are one seed and all arms pre-existed the audit; this is a post-hoc characterisation with pre-registered quantities, not a prospective test. Code: scripts/audit_conditioning.py , tests in scripts/test_conditioning.py ; per-arm values in results/conditioning_audit/audit.json .

sections.heading: Appendix X A physics conjunct outside every score

The repository’s print-and-fire readiness screen does: Bartz throat heat flux at the operating point the requirement implies ( p c = F / ( C F ​ A t ) = 1.30 p_{c}=F/(C_{F}A_{t})=1.30 bar for every requirement, since r t ∝ F r_{t}\propto\sqrt{F} ; ϕ = 1 \phi=1 , T c = 2287 T_{c}=2287 K, c ∗ = 1249 c^{*}=1249 m/s, within 1.1 % 1.1\% of the repository’s Cantera values); a closed-form steady hot face through the liner, cooled by regenerative air at 9 bar through the body’s own cooling-zone channels (film coefficient from the air velocity in the channels that fit mid-wall); von Mises margin against the AlSi10Mg yield at the hot-face temperature; and a Coffin–Manson low-cycle-fatigue life of at least 20 20 fires. sections.heading: The conjunct binds, and its lever is the cooling channels.
sections.text: Among feasible bodies, 29 29 – 64 % 64\% survive. The hot face is set by the coolant film coefficient, i.e. by the total channel flow area A cool = n ​ π ​ r eff 2 A_{\rm cool}=n\pi r_{\rm eff}^{2} : more or wider channels slow the air and heat the wall. This is the metal that mass minimisation removes. The 7B gated policy, whose mass tracks the budget with gain 0.62 0.62 (Appendix W ), opens 86 86 mm 2 against the sum policy’s 51 51 mm 2 and runs its median hot face at 604 ∘ 604^{\circ} C against 409 ∘ 409^{\circ} C, so 0.31 0.31 of its feasible bodies survive against 0.54 0.54 . Latent search, the best generator under the original target ( 0.375 0.375 per draw, supply 0.94 0.94 ), opens 116 116 mm 2 , runs at 1114 ∘ 1114^{\circ} C and survives at 0.18 0.18 . The two critic-trained decoders have no cooling zone in 100 % 100\% of their designs — the printability rule that penalises a channel against its ligament is satisfied by deleting the channels — and zero survival.

sections.heading: What the training rules protect is what the score ranks.
sections.text: Under the extended target, on target ∧ \wedge ready, the gate’s composed advantage over the sum shrinks at 1.5B ( 0.296 0.296 against 0.260 0.260 ; supply 0.444 0.444 against 0.371 0.371 ) and inverts on two of three seeds at 7B ( 0.203 0.203 against 0.231 0.231 ; supply 0.249 0.249 against 0.268 0.268 ). Survival among feasible bodies is higher than the base’s on every trained DPO arm ( 12 / 12 12/12 ), but the ordering between rules is not stable across scales. We had registered that the gate would keep its advantage on every seed at both scales; it does not, and the reversal at 7B is the informative miss. The selection side is more robust: the two-stage screen, which sees no physics, still captures η ext = 0.51 \eta_{\rm ext}=0.51 – 0.86 0.86 of the attainable extended lift, because feasibility and mass are necessary conditions; the same rule given the readiness verdict as one more conjunct reaches 0.87 0.87 – 0.97 0.97 . The feasibility head’s own ordering against the physics bin is not at chance ( A phys A_{\rm phys} 0.44 0.44 – 0.69 0.69 ; three-bin identity exact to 2 × 10 − 16 2\times 10^{-16} ), which is the wall–ligament coupling, not knowledge of heat transfer.

sections.heading: Registered predictions and misses.
sections.text: Eight predictions were written before the audit ( context/docs/PLAN_PHYSICS_GATE_2026-09-18.md ). Held: every trained DPO arm survives better than its base; the identity is exact; A phys A_{\rm phys} on gated 1.5B is 0.554 0.554 against a registered 0.55 0.55 ; η ext \eta_{\rm ext} on gated 1.5B is 0.557 0.557 against 0.55 0.55 . Missed: every absolute survival rate (we predicted 0.45 0.45 – 0.65 0.65 and measured 0.29 0.29 – 0.41 0.41 ; the screen is harsher on AlSi10Mg than the CuCrZr numbers we calibrated on); gate above sum on every seed (reversed at 7B); supply and answer under the extended target for gated 1.5B ( 0.444 0.444 and 0.296 0.296 against 0.55 0.55 and 0.35 0.35 ); latent search survival ( 0.18 0.18 against 0.50 0.50 ); and that no trained policy sets its wall from the thrust — the sum-ranked and GRPO policies do (partial correlation 0.30 0.30 – 0.63 0.63 ), through the bore radii that printability depends on, while the gated 1.5B policy does not ( 0.01 0.01 – 0.08 0.08 ). All arms in the paragraphs above pre-existed the audit. Code: scripts/audit_physics_gate.py ; per-arm values and the declared operating point in results/physics_gate_audit/audit.json .

sections.heading: The policies that track mass hardest run hottest.
sections.text: The four arms trained afterwards ( † \dagger in Table 22 ) were screened with predictions registered first ( PLAN_NEW_ARMS_CPU_2026-09-19.md ). The two rules whose pairs contrast mass and not feasibility open the widest channels ( 93 93 and 104 104 mm 2 against the gate’s 59 59 ), run at 692 692 and 719 ∘ 719^{\circ} C, and survive at 0.28 0.28 – 0.29 0.29 among feasible bodies, below the gate on every seed and at the base’s level; the log-probability form sits with the sum ( 0.42 0.42 ; registered within 0.05 0.05 of it). The registered claim that every trained arm survives better than the base in absolute terms fails on two of twelve seeds (tuned sum and mass-only, at 0.26 0.26 – 0.27 0.27 against the base’s 0.28 0.28 ), because those policies never installed the feasibility that survival rides on.

sections.heading: The gate composes conjuncts, at a price.
sections.text: Putting the readiness verdict into the gate — pairs ranked by mass_term − 100 [ prob < 0.5 ] − 100 [ ¬ ready ] -100\,[\texttt{prob}<0.5]-100\,[\lnot\text{ready}] , the readiness label computed for the stored train pool in seconds, the recipe otherwise unchanged — and training three seeds ( PLAN_PHYSICS_DPO_2026-09-18.md , registered before the job) raises survival among feasible bodies from 0.40 0.40 to 0.55 0.55 ( 0.52 0.52 – 0.57 0.57 , every seed above the two-conjunct gate), the extended composed answer from 0.30 0.30 to 0.37 0.37 , and the physics-aware ceiling from 0.41 0.41 to 0.46 0.46 , with mass tracking intact (gain 1.04 1.04 – 1.08 1.08 ) and printability at ceiling. Of eleven registered checks seven held and four missed, all in the direction of a smaller effect: survival 0.55 0.55 against a registered 0.60 0.60 , extended per-draw 0.135 0.135 against 0.20 0.20 , extended supply 0.50 0.50 against 0.60 0.60 ; the falsifier (survival below 0.45 0.45 ) did not fire. The miss that says most: the policy’s channel area still does not depend on the thrust ( 0.30 → 0.31 0.30\to 0.31 partial correlation), so it improved survival unconditionally — channels 59 → 40 59\to 40 mm 2 , median hot face 485 → 365 ∘ 485\to 365^{\circ} C — rather than by learning the coolant requirement the thrust implies, the same pattern as the unconditional shortcut in Appendix W . The price is paid on the original target: per-draw 0.311 → 0.257 0.311\to 0.257 , supply 0.81 → 0.74 0.81\to 0.74 , composed 0.76 → 0.69 0.76\to 0.69 . The feasibility head’s mixture terms are unchanged ( q q 0.946 0.946 , A own A_{\rm own} 0.958 0.958 ). Artifacts: reproduced/physics_gate_dpo/ ; code scripts/summarize_physics_gate_dpo.py .

sections.heading: Purpose.
sections.text: This study was designed after the original engine results as an external stress test, not as an exploratory search for another positive domain. The benchmark, critic, model revisions, pair builders, scalar grids, DPO recipe, primary endpoint, equivalence margin, and 30-run matrix were frozen before confirmatory DPO. The optional INCART OOD phase was disabled before the primary freeze and was not run. The freeze is an internal commitment: protocol, manifest and predictions are SHA-256 hashed in the project repository (freeze commit f0b5895 ) before any confirmatory DPO run, but were not deposited with an external registry, so their timing rests on the repository history rather than on a third-party timestamp.

sections.heading: Data and split.
sections.text: The primary signals are MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database v1.0.0 (DOI 10.13026/C2F305), with baseline-wander, muscle-artifact and electrode-motion recordings from MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database v1.0.0. Records 201 and 202 are grouped as one subject. Subjects are split before window construction into 27 train, 8 validation and 12 test subjects, yielding 1,000/300/500 fixed 30-s requirements. Beat annotations are used only for eligibility and the biomedical oracle and do not enter the prompt features.

sections.heading: Pipeline DSL and target.
sections.text: Each generator emits a finite causal ECG pipeline with whitelisted high-pass and low-pass settings, filter family, notch setting, downsampling, derivative flag, integration window, adaptive threshold multiplier, refractory period and numeric format. The deployment label is F = valid/stable ∧ [ cycles ≤ C r ] ∧ [ RAM ≤ R r ] ∧ [ latency ≤ L r ] . F=\text{valid/stable}\wedge[\mathrm{cycles}\leq C_{r}]\wedge[\mathrm{RAM}\leq R_{r}]\wedge[\mathrm{latency}\leq L_{r}]. The biomedical label is M = [ F 1 QRS ≥ 0.80 ] ∧ [ MAE R ≤ 65 ms ] , M=[F1_{\rm QRS}\geq 0.80]\wedge[\mathrm{MAE}_{R}\leq 65\text{ ms}], and the full target is y = F ∧ M y=F\wedge M . Benchmark difficulty was resolved from 131,072 Sobol configurations before generator experiments: P ⁡ ( F ) = 0.5848 P(F)=0.5848 , P ⁡ ( M ∣ F ) = 0.2408 P(M\mid F)=0.2408 , with semantic counts 54,421 F = 0 F=0 , 58,192 F = 1 , M = 0 F=1,M=0 , and 18,459 F = 1 , M = 1 F=1,M=1 .

sections.heading: Fixed critic.
sections.text: One two-head MLP critic is trained independently of the generator families and then frozen. Its held-out test AUC is 1.000 for feasibility and 0.930 for utility. The same critic scores Llama, Gemma and Phi candidate pools.

sections.heading: Models and generation.
sections.text: The frozen generator revisions are Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (revision 0cb88a4... ), Gemma-3-4B-IT ( 093f9f3... ), and Phi-4-mini-instruct ( cfbefac... ). Each requirement has K = 16 K=16 samples at temperature 0.8 and top- p = 0.95 p=0.95 . The first prompt implementation was rejected before the preregistration freeze because it produced no usable Gemma outputs and almost no schema-valid Llama outputs; no valid biomedical outcomes from that attempt were available for scientific tuning. A shared prompt-v2 was accepted by a parse-only train pilot under a criterion fixed before inspecting those outputs, then hashed and frozen. The Phi checkpoint required disabling incompatible remote model code before any model weights or completions were produced; all scientific settings remained unchanged. These engineering deviations are retained in the package.

sections.heading: Selection and pair construction.
sections.text: The scalar grid is { .001 , .003 , .01 , .03 , .1 , .3 , 1 , 3 , 10 } \{.001,.003,.01,.03,.1,.3,1,3,10\} . Validation selection gives w sel = .003 , .001 , .03 w_{\rm sel}=.003,.001,.03 for Llama, Gemma and Phi. A critic-only normalized maximin of chosen/rejected feasibility and utility contrasts on the frozen train pools (each contrast divided by its maximum over the grid; the gate-free criterion of Appendix O ) gives w pair = 1 , .1 , .3 w_{\rm pair}=1,.1,.3 . Each rule constructs 4,000 deterministic top-4-versus-bottom-4 pairs. Llama additionally includes a unit-sum arm. Exact pair overlap with the hard gate is 92.3%/25.6% for Llama inference/pair weights, 99.5%/71.1% for Gemma, and 79.6%/31.0% for Phi. Llama pair-weight and unit-sum pairs are exactly identical.

sections.heading: DPO and evaluation.
sections.text: All runs use sigmoid DPO with β = .1 \beta=.1 , two epochs, learning rate 10 − 5 10^{-5} , LoRA rank 16 ( α = 32 \alpha=32 , dropout .05), batch 2 with accumulation 8, and maximum length 768. The matrix contains 12 Llama runs and 9 each for Gemma and Phi, three seeds per rule. All 30 runs completed and all 30 aligned test pools contain 500 requirements by 16 candidates. Evaluation uses one common hard-feasibility-then-utility selector, not the training rule. The primary endpoint is Answer@16; the preregistered gate-equivalence margin is ± .04 \pm.04 .

sections.text: Table 25 lists all 30 runs. No seed was removed or repeated. sections.heading: Sensitivity to the number of test subjects (post-hoc).
sections.text: The frozen bootstrap resamples only 12 test subjects. A leave-one-subject-out jackknife with t 11 t_{11} intervals gives [ − .386 , − .273 ] [-.386,-.273] , [ + .043 , + .194 ] [+.043,+.194] and [ − .264 , − .128 ] [-.264,-.128] for pair minus inference (Llama, Gemma, Phi), [ − .390 , − .283 ] [-.390,-.283] , [ + .043 , + .194 ] [+.043,+.194] and [ − .253 , − .131 ] [-.253,-.131] for pair minus gate, and [ − .003 , + .016 ] [-.003,+.016] , [ − .002 , + .001 ] [-.002,+.001] and [ − .018 , + .010 ] [-.018,+.010] for gate minus inference. Dropping any single subject moves no estimate by more than 0.024 0.024 . Per-seed contrasts are the informative caveat: pair minus gate is − .21 , − .19 , − .18 -.21,-.19,-.18 for Phi, but − .51 , − .52 , + .02 -.51,-.52,+.02 for Llama and − .01 , + .12 , + .24 -.01,+.12,+.24 for Gemma, so only the Phi sign is stable across training seeds.

sections.heading: Output diversity and a requirement-blind program (post-hoc).
sections.text: One pipeline (IIR4 filter, 0.5–25 Hz band, no notch, no downsampling, derivative on, 140 ms integration, threshold multiplier 0.35, 220 ms refractory, Q15 arithmetic) satisfies the full target on 51.2 % 51.2\% of test requirements regardless of the request. It is already the most frequent Llama base output ( 38.5 % 38.5\% of train samples). It accounts for 78 78 – 100 % 100\% of parsed outputs in six of the eight Llama arms that parse, and for 97.1 97.1 – 100 % 100\% of parsed outputs in all three Phi pair-weight seeds, versus 0 0 – 8 % 8\% in Phi gate and inference arms, which retain 79–113 distinct pipelines per 500 × \times 16 pool. Gemma never emits it. Endpoints near 0.512 0.512 therefore indicate a requirement-blind policy, not partial success.

sections.heading: Gate-referenced versus gate-free contrast criteria (post-hoc).
sections.text: Rebuilding the pairs of the frozen builder on the frozen train pools for every grid weight (which reproduces the frozen gate pair sets exactly), the critic contrasts at the gate coincide with those of the smallest weights: the gate’s feasibility contrast is matched within 1.2 % 1.2\% at w ≤ 0.01 w\leq 0.01 in every family, while its utility contrast equals the sweep maximum within 0.2 % 0.2\% . The gate-free maximin therefore moves away from the gate toward feasibility. Selecting instead the grid weight nearest the gate in gate-normalized critic-contrast space gives w = 0.01 w=0.01 (Llama), 0.003 0.003 (Gemma) and 0.003 0.003 (Phi), with exact pair overlap with the gate of 87.3 % 87.3\% , 99.0 % 99.0\% and 94.7 % 94.7\% . At w pair w_{\rm pair} , the oracle utility contrast falls from .524 .524 to .461 .461 (Llama) and from .303 .303 to .259 .259 (Phi) relative to the gate, while the oracle feasibility contrast is unchanged or slightly higher. No policy was trained with the gate-referenced weights; these numbers locate the criteria, they are not training outcomes.

sections.heading: Interpretation.
sections.text: The study supports transfer of the audit and selection separations and the pair-equivalence reading of the training interface. It rejects the gate-free contrast criterion as a transferable recipe; in its one informative family (Phi) the failure has the engine’s feasibility-dominated signature and ends in a requirement-blind program. It does not establish that gate-referenced contrast matching would succeed outside the near-identical-pair regime.

sections.heading: Appendix AA Audit, selection and reranker analyses: proofs and CPU-only results
sections.text: All analyses in this appendix are post hoc, CPU-only, and use the frozen ECG pools, the frozen critic and the frozen common evaluator; scripts are v23_*.py and v24_*.py in the supplement. No policy was trained for this appendix.

sections.heading: Mixture-shift versus ordering-drift decomposition.
sections.text: Across two policies, the AUC change can also be decomposed into mixture shift and conditional-ordering drift: A t − A s = \displaystyle A_{t}-A_{s}={} ( q t − q s ) ​ ( A cross s − A own s ) \displaystyle(q_{t}-q_{s})(A_{\rm cross}^{s}-A_{\rm own}^{s}) (7) + ( 1 − q t ) ​ ( A own t − A own s ) + q t ​ ( A cross t − A cross s ) . \displaystyle+(1-q_{t})(A_{\rm own}^{t}-A_{\rm own}^{s})+q_{t}(A_{\rm cross}^{t}-A_{\rm cross}^{s}). The first term changes only composition; the last two change conditional ordering. Both mechanisms can therefore coexist. The identity extends to any disjoint failure-bin partition and requires no independence assumptions.

sections.heading: Rules that reduce the saturated component’s influence recover selection.
sections.text: Holding the candidate pools and critic fixed, the raw unit sum reaches η = 0.10 ± 0.02 \eta=0.10\pm 0.02 on matched 1.5B pools, rank averaging 0.58 ± 0.01 0.58\pm 0.01 , a validation-tuned feasibility weight of 0.005 0.005 reaches 0.88 ± 0.02 0.88\pm 0.02 , the soft log-probability rule reaches 0.89 ± 0.00 0.89\pm 0.00 , and threshold-then-mass reaches 0.92 ± 0.01 0.92\pm 0.01 . At 7B, the raw sum remains poor ( 0.05 ± 0.02 0.05\pm 0.02 ) while threshold-then-mass reaches 0.94 ± 0.04 0.94\pm 0.04 (full sweep in Appendix M ). The residual feasibility ordering is not useless (permuting it within the passing set lowers raw-sum answer on gated 7B pools from 0.237 0.237 to 0.209 0.209 , post-hoc); the problem is excessive influence, not absence of cross-signal.

sections.heading: Controls.
sections.text: A holistic on-target classifier (held-out AUC 0.974 0.974 ) avoids the component-AUC cliff but captures only η = 0.49 \eta=0.49 – 0.60 0.60 , versus 0.90 0.90 – 0.94 0.94 for the gated two-head critic. This is not evidence that decomposition is universally superior: the mass regressor contains ordinal distance-to-budget information. GSM8K shows the opposite saturation geometry. Its format-head within-pool SD falls from 8.6 8.6 to 0.02 0.02 , so the tested composites effectively reduce to the correctness head and agree within 0.01 0.01 (Appendix C ).
