sections.heading: AD.2 Protocol
sections.text: Data are the frozen ECG pools of Appendix Z : base-policy train pools (Llama, Phi), base-policy test pools (Llama, Phi, and Gemma as an unseen generator), and the test pools of the six post-DPO policies per family trained with gate or inference-weight pairs. Features are the frozen critic’s 55 55 inputs (requirement descriptors and one-hot DSL fields). Head classes: an MLP with the critic’s architecture ( 256 256 - 128 128 - 64 64 , Adam, batch 256 256 , up to 40 40 epochs) and histogram gradient boosting ( 200 200 trees, no early stopping). Label-mixture heads (P1) are trained from scratch on the base train pool with each candidate duplicated and labelled y y with probability λ \lambda and F F otherwise, for three seeds. Refresh heads continue training the specialist S S ( λ = 0 \lambda=0 ): the MLP by 20 20 epochs of partial_fit , the GBM by 100 100 additional trees on the refresh data. Refresh data are all parsed candidates of the post-DPO pools whose requirement belongs to a random half of the test subjects (seeds 100 100 – 109 109 ); R mix R_{\rm mix} adds an equal number of base-train candidates drawn uniformly. All metrics use the complementary subject half. The monitor is the within-pool full-target AUC of Section 2 , averaged over the six post-DPO policies; canonical F F -AUC is computed over all parsed candidates of the base pools; the gate selects the highest frozen utility score among candidates with head probability ≥ 0.5 \geq 0.5 and otherwise the head’s top candidate.

sections.heading: AD.3 Where the interface ingredients already appear
sections.text: The exact controller we analyze is a composition of interfaces, not a claim about one named product. Table 34 records the closest modern ingredients. Rubric systems expose criterion-level judgments but ultimately aggregate them for policy optimization; policy-aware rubric work explicitly measures saturation; and separate reward-model work refreshes models from fresh policy-interaction data. At LLM scale, POW3R reports 17 17 – 26 % 26\% saturated and 20 20 – 33 % 33\% dead rubric criteria across its fresh-policy diagnostics, so criterion informativeness is visibly policy-dependent even before any maintenance decision is made ( Tyagi et al., 2026 ) . The unsafe loop arises when an aggregate outcome statistic is reused as the maintenance signal for one component head. sections.heading: AD.6 Natural multi-label semantic stress test: GoEmotions
sections.text: We use the official GoEmotions development and test splits ( Demszky et al., 2020 ) , with 5,426 5{,}426 and 5,427 5{,}427 Reddit comments. Each comment can carry multiple human-annotated emotion labels. The component F F is fixed throughout as absence of annoyance ; the development/test sets contain 303 / 320 303/320 annoyance-labelled own failures. We train Laplace-smoothed multinomial Naive Bayes heads on the development split over a fixed bag-of-words vocabulary (terms occurring at least twice; at most 10,000 10{,}000 ). This small transparent model is intentional: the experiment tests the audit geometry without conflating it with a large verifier’s capacity.

sections.heading: Support depletion and targeted replay.
sections.text: We next retrain the correct F F classifier while retaining all F = 1 F=1 development examples and a nested number of annoyance-labelled failures. Canonical F F -AUC rises from .537 .537 with two own failures to .545 .545 (8), .594 .594 (64), .638 .638 (128), .671 .671 (256), and .679 .679 with all 303 303 failures. The original fixed 8+80 own-failure replay arm reaches .615 .615 . To distinguish targeted failure support from generic extra data, we additionally repeat 100 deterministic draws. Adding 80 random development examples to the 8-failure arm adds only 4.42 ± 1.96 4.42\pm 1.96 own failures on average and raises canonical F F -AUC only to .550 ± .004 .550\pm.004 . Adding 80 targeted own failures instead reaches .606 ± .008 .606\pm.008 . At the development-set prevalence, a uniform sample would require about 1,433 1{,}433 examples in expectation to contain 80 own failures. The rescue is therefore about reconstructing the missing semantic support, not merely increasing the update set. Figure 14: Failure-targeted replay is sample-efficient. Starting from only eight own failures, 80 indiscriminate examples add few relevant failures and barely move canonical F F -AUC; 80 explicit own failures recover substantially more component discrimination. Error bars show SD over 100 deterministic replay draws; the full-support bar uses all 303 development failures. sections.heading: Appendix AE Selection interface: audit equivalence does not imply equal influence
sections.text: The audit in Section 4 uses only the ordering within one component score, so it is invariant to every strictly increasing reparameterization s F ↦ g ⁡ ( s F ) s_{F}\mapsto g(s_{F}) . A multi-component selector also consumes the scale of s F s_{F} relative to the other heads. The next result characterizes exactly how much of the selector’s decision the audit leaves open. Proposition 5 (Selection ambiguity is the Pareto set) . Fix a pool with component scores ( s F , s M ) (s_{F},s_{M}) and distinct score pairs (duplicates are merged; Appendix Y ). As g g ranges over strictly increasing maps—all of which leave every ROC/AUC of s F s_{F} unchanged—the set of top-1 choices of g ⁡ ( s F ) + s M g(s_{F})+s_{M} is exactly the Pareto set Par \operatorname{Par} of the pool in ( s F , s M ) (s_{F},s_{M}) . Over positive rescalings g ⁡ ( t ) = c ​ t g(t)=ct it is the subset of Par \operatorname{Par} on the upper convex hull. Hence an audit statistic invariant to monotone reparameterization determines the composite decision iff | Par | = 1 |\operatorname{Par}|=1 , and determines whether that decision is on target iff all Pareto candidates share one oracle label. The proof is constructive (Appendix Y ): a dominated candidate loses under every increasing g g , and each Pareto candidate wins under a g g that jumps at its own s F s_{F} . This is the classical correspondence between Pareto optimality and monotone scalarization ( Miettinen, 1999 ) , read here as a statement about what an audit leaves open. Its size is predictable. Proposition 6 (Ambiguity grows with pool size) . If the K K candidates’ score pairs are i.i.d. with continuous, independent s F s_{F} and s M s_{M} , then | Par | |\operatorname{Par}| is a sum of independent Bernoulli ( 1 / i ) (1/i) variables, i = 1 , … , K i=1,\ldots,K . Hence 𝔼 ​ | Par | = H K = ln ⁡ K + 0.577 + o ⁡ ( 1 ) \mathbb{E}|\operatorname{Par}|=H_{K}=\ln K+0.577+o(1) and Pr [ | Par | = 1 ] = 1 / K \Pr[|\operatorname{Par}|=1]=1/K . If the heads are comonotone, | Par | = 1 |\operatorname{Par}|=1 . Sorting candidates by decreasing s F s_{F} , a candidate is Pareto iff its s M s_{M} is a running maximum, which happens with probability 1 / i 1/i independently across i i ( Bentley et al., 1978 ) . Under independent heads the audit therefore determines the best-of- K K decision with probability only 1 / K 1/K , which vanishes as test-time compute grows; in our pools positively dependent heads slow this growth without stopping it (Figure 16 a). Figure 16: (a) With every component AUC fixed, the range of Answer@ K K reachable by audit-equivalent composites on the ECG base test pools grows with K K (Proposition 6 ; 20 20 subsamples per pool). (b) Endpoint minus hard gate against exact pair overlap for all eleven trained scalar rules (engine 1.5B and ECG; three seeds each; common evaluator). Filled: families whose gate clears the requirement-blind floor (engine, Phi); open: uninformative (Llama near the blind pipeline, Gemma without supply); this post-hoc split uses only each family’s gate arm, never a rule’s gap (Appendix AB ). All three rules with overlap ≥ 0.79 \geq 0.79 match the gate within 0.007 0.007 (two in uninformative families); five of six informative low-overlap rules miss by ≥ 0.08 \geq 0.08 , the exception being the contrast-matched w = 0.1 w=0.1 .

sections.text: On matched 1.5B DPO pools, rescaling the feasibility logit by c ∈ { 0.01 , … , 100 } c\in\{0.01,\ldots,100\} leaves its AUC unchanged but moves raw-sum best-of-16 from 0.544 0.544 to 0.160 0.160 (Appendix M ); the unit sum follows the saturated logit on 82 % 82\% of pools ( η = 0.10 \eta=0.10 ). sections.heading: Takeaway.
sections.text: Component AUC fixes the order within a score; the selector’s decision is fixed only up to the Pareto set, whose size and label mix at the deployed K K should be reported alongside any component audit. A weight tuned for this interface is a selection weight ; Section AF shows why that does not make it a training weight.

sections.heading: Appendix AF Training interface: a good selector need not build good DPO data
sections.text: Once a score constructs preference data, DPO sees only the chosen/rejected pairs, so selection quality and training-pair quality are different objectives even for one scalar ranking rule. Proposition 7 (What reaches DPO) . Fix pools, policy, reference model, β \beta , and a deterministic rank-based pair builder. (i) The empirical DPO objective and gradient depend on the scoring rule only through the induced pair multiset; for r w = w ​ s F + s M r_{w}=ws_{F}+s_{M} this multiset is piecewise constant in w w , changing only at crossing weights w i ​ j = − ( s M , i − s M , j ) / ( s F , i − s F , j ) w_{ij}=-(s_{M,i}-s_{M,j})/(s_{F,i}-s_{F,j}) . (ii) Neither component-order nor top- k k equivalence implies pair equivalence when the builder uses ranks outside the top k k . (iii) For uniform pair multisets P , Q P,Q of equal size, d TV ​ ( P , Q ) = 1 − overlap ⁡ ( P , Q ) d_{\rm TV}(P,Q)=1-\mathrm{overlap}(P,Q) ; if the preference log-ratio satisfies | d θ | ≤ R |d_{\theta}|\leq R and per-pair gradients are bounded by G G , then | L P − L Q | ≤ β ​ R ​ ( 1 − overlap ) |L_{P}-L_{Q}|\leq\beta R\,(1-\mathrm{overlap}) and ‖ ∇ L P − ∇ L Q ‖ ≤ 2 ​ G ​ ( 1 − overlap ) \|\nabla L_{P}-\nabla L_{Q}\|\leq 2G\,(1-\mathrm{overlap}) . (iv) If both objectives are convex and L L -smooth, full-batch gradient descent with step η ≤ 2 / L \eta\leq 2/L from a common initialization satisfies ‖ θ T P − θ T Q ‖ ≤ 2 ​ η ​ G ​ T ​ ( 1 − overlap ) \|\theta^{P}_{T}-\theta^{Q}_{T}\|\leq 2\eta GT\,(1-\mathrm{overlap}) ; with L L -smoothness alone the factor η ​ T \eta T becomes ( ( 1 + η ​ L ) T − 1 ) / L ((1+\eta L)^{T}-1)/L . Together with Proposition 5 , this gives a strict hierarchy: composite order determines the pair multiset, which determines the DPO objective; component order determines neither, and a good top- k k selector need not fix the pairs (Appendix Q gives a two-candidate example). Exact pair overlap therefore certifies closeness of the objective, of its gradient and, under (iv), of short training trajectories; because the trajectory bound grows with the horizon ( Hardt et al., 2016 ) , overlap certifies objectives, and endpoints only when it is near one. Mean property contrasts are only a projection of the pair distribution with an unmeasured residual (Proposition 4 ).

sections.heading: Frozen outcome.
sections.text: The preregistered primary outcome is negative for our criterion: pair weighting is gate-equivalent in no family (Table 40 ). In Gemma it even exceeds the gate ( + 0.119 +0.119 ), but no Gemma arm approaches the requirement-blind pipeline (best seed 0.244 0.244 vs 0.512 0.512 ), so this is not evidence for the criterion. Gate and inference weight differ by at most 0.007 0.007 with 79.6 79.6 – 99.5 % 99.5\% shared pairs. With training seeds resampled together with subjects, only Phi’s pair deficit stays clear of zero (Appendices Z , AA ). Llama’s w pair = 1 w_{\rm pair}=1 pairs are identical to those of an added unit-sum arm, and both fail to parse on two seeds, a shared collapse rather than a test of Proposition 7 .

sections.heading: What the endpoints mean (post-hoc).
sections.text: Llama arms that parse mostly emit the requirement-blind pipeline ( 0.512 0.512 ), and Gemma has near-zero supply. In Phi, gate and inference policies keep 79–113 distinct pipelines, whereas all pair-weight seeds collapse onto the blind program ( ≥ 97 % \geq 97\% of parsed outputs). The gate-free criterion fails because in ECG the gate sits at the M M -heavy end of the sweep, so normalizing by sweep maxima pushes toward F F ; a gate-referenced criterion would select w = 0.003 w=0.003 – 0.01 0.01 with 87 87 – 99 % 99\% gate overlap.

sections.heading: A trained check on CPU.
sections.text: We trained a log-linear DPO reranker on the frozen Llama and Phi pools, where DPO is convex and Proposition 7 (iv) applies exactly: gate and nine grid weights, ten seeds each, with design and four predictions hashed before any run (Appendix AA ). All four held: the gate-referenced weight matches the gate ( + 0.004 +0.004 [ − 0.005 , 0.015 ] [-0.005,0.015] ; − 0.002 -0.002 [ − 0.007 , 0.002 ] [-0.007,0.002] ); Phi’s gate-free weight is not shown equivalent and, like the LLM policies, shifts top-1 choices onto the blind program ( 67 % 67\% vs 25 % 25\% ); across the grid | | gap | | shrinks as overlap grows (Spearman of | | gap | | on overlap − 0.60 -0.60 , − 0.93 -0.93 ); and parameter distances respect the bound. The reranker has little headroom above the blind program, so it corroborates direction and ordering, not LLM effect sizes. Where gate pairs can be built, training on them is simpler than any gate-referenced scalar.

sections.heading: Takeaway.
sections.text: Inference scalarization is a decision rule; pre-DPO scalarization is a data-construction operator . The evidence is one-directional and thin (Figure 16 b, Appendix AB ): all three rules with ≥ 79 % \geq 79\% gate overlap reached the gate’s endpoint, consistent with Proposition 7 , but only Phi’s comes from a family whose gate is informative; low overlap left the endpoint undetermined. A weak bottleneck contrast accompanied all four informative misses, but Phi’s pair weight also missed with balanced contrasts, a residual that two contrast coordinates cannot see. In practice: when a tuned selection weight trains poorly, check its pair overlap with the rule it should emulate; if overlap is low, neither overlap nor mean contrasts certify it, and the reference rule’s own pairs are the safe default.

We study a specific control loop: a component verifier is evaluated on fresh policy outputs against the full success label and refreshed when that aggregate score falls. For a conjunctive target y = F ∧ M y=F\wedge M , its on-policy AUC is ( 1 − q ) ​ A own + q ​ A cross (1-q)A_{\rm own}+qA_{\rm cross} , where q = Pr ⁡ [ F = 1 ∣ y = 0 ] q=\Pr[F=1\mid y=0] . As the policy masters F F , q q can rise toward one, removing weight from F F -failures and rewarding information about M M . We call this on-policy audit collapse . We derive a sharp identified set, a complete-erasure threshold, and the exact point at which the audit can prefer a worse component verifier; its population optimum is the full-outcome predictor, not the component oracle. An exact oracle exhibits the collapse, a natural multi-label text control shows inversion can select a head with lower canonical F F -AUC at the observed failure mixture, and a prediction-registered ECG study shows that acting on the audit can reduce off-policy F F -AUC, transfer the damage to an unseen generator, and increase downstream constraint violations. Preserving own-failure support prevents the damage. Matching label-complexity bounds and a controlled-mixture audit give the corresponding repair: audit the component on its own failures, and keep those failures in the refresh distribution. 1 Introduction Verifier stacks increasingly sit inside the optimization loop. Post-training systems combine outcome, process, rubric and constraint signals, while test-time compute uses verifier scores to search, rank and select candidates ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ; Lightman et al., 2024 ; Brown et al., 2024 ; Snell et al., 2025 ; Mahmoud et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2023 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ; Moskovitz et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2026 ; Bai et al., 2026 ) . A natural but unsafe control loop is to monitor a component verifier on fresh policy samples against the full task outcome; if that aggregate score drops, collect new on-policy data and refresh the verifier. Policy-interaction data are in fact used to refine reward models and iterative RLHF pipelines repeatedly update preference models on fresh policy data ( Bai et al., 2022 ; Sun et al., 2025 ) . This paper shows that this loop can become systematically wrong because the policy improved . Let success require y = F ∧ M y=F\wedge M and let s F s_{F} be a verifier intended to score F F . Among failures, some violate F F and others already satisfy F F but fail only M M . Pairwise additivity of AUC gives AUC ⁡ ( s F ; y ) = ( 1 − q ) ​ A own + q ​ A cross , q = Pr ⁡ [ F = 1 ∣ y = 0 ] . \operatorname{AUC}(s_{F};y)=(1-q)A_{\rm own}+qA_{\rm cross},\qquad q=\Pr[F=1\mid y=0]. (1) Here A own A_{\rm own} is the audit’s own-failure separability : target successes versus F F -failures. It is not, in general, identical to canonical F F -AUC; Section 2 separates the two estimands explicitly. A cross A_{\rm cross} compares successes with failures that already satisfy F F ; an exact F F -oracle has A cross = 1 / 2 A_{\rm cross}=1/2 by construction. When optimization increases satisfaction of F F faster than the remaining conjunct—in particular as F F saturates while M M remains imperfect— q q rises. Consequently, the standard aggregate monitor progressively removes weight from the verifier’s own failure mode and places it on information about the other conjunct. The paradox is therefore directional: the more completely the policy masters a component, the less the usual on-policy audit measures that component. We call this on-policy audit collapse : optimization removes the very failure mode needed to evaluate the module that learned it. This creates a concrete failure chain. First, the monitor loses identification: a falling AUC need not imply a worse component verifier. Second, it can become actively anti-aligned with the audit’s intended subproblem: at a calculable q ∗ q^{\ast} it prefers a head with worse A own A_{\rm own} because that head leaks information about M M ; in our text and engine controls this can also select a head with worse canonical F F -AUC. Third, the usual response to a bad monitor—on-policy refresh—can remove component competence. Once optimization has depleted F F -failures, refresh data alone no longer identify the boundary the component verifier must retain; outcome labels can actively entangle it, while even correct F F labels cannot reconstruct failures absent from support. The result can look benign on the monitored distribution while becoming worse exactly on the off-support failures a constraint checker must catch after a generator, prompt distribution, or policy shift. policy learns F F F F -failures vanish q ↑ q\!\uparrow audit changes meaning cross-signal wins refresh can forget F F Viewed as a learning system, this is a control-plane failure: optimizing the policy changes the data used to decide whether its verifier should be replaced or refreshed. When does the failure apply? The central result requires three ingredients: a head intended for component F F , an on-policy audit against the full outcome y y rather than a component-specific label, and use of that audit to compare, early-stop or trigger refreshes. If trusted F F labels are available and the component is audited directly (preferably on a reference distribution that preserves F F -failures), the collapse in Eq. 1 is avoided. Our claim is therefore about this specific but natural interface, not about every verifier evaluation protocol. Why this interface is current. Its ingredients already coexist in modern post-training systems. Rubric RL independently scores prompt-specific criteria and aggregates them into a scalar on-policy reward ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ; Mahmoud et al., 2026 ) ; policy-aware rubric work reports that substantial criterion mass is already saturated or dead under current policies ( Tyagi et al., 2026 ) ; and fresh policy-interaction data are used to refine reward models or preference models ( Sun et al., 2025 ; Bai et al., 2022 ) . We do not claim that these systems implement our exact audit-trigger-refresh controller end to end. They establish that criterion-level verifiers, policy-induced saturation, scalar aggregation and on-policy refinement are contemporary ingredients; Appendix AD.3 maps the interfaces explicitly. Our experiments are organized to test this chain rather than to accumulate unrelated benchmarks. The engine domain gives an exact component oracle, allowing us to separate real verifier failure from a case-mix artifact. GSM8K supplies a familiar language-domain negative control for ranking inversion. A natural multi-label GoEmotions stress test uses separately annotated semantic criteria to test audit collapse, inversion and refresh under support depletion; a constructed AG News control is reported in the appendix. ECG then stresses the operational consequence on a frozen external benchmark with three generator families, subject-held-out splits, two refresh model classes, downstream best-of- 16 16 selection, and a precommitted set of predictions. Across these settings the observations line up with the mechanism: exact-oracle AUC collapses, the analytic inversion threshold predicts where inversion does and does not occur, optimization removes own-failure support, outcome refresh damages off-policy canonical F F -AUC and downstream constraints in every paired split, and deliberately restoring failure support prevents the damage. Contributions. (1) On-policy audit collapse. We derive the mixture law, a sharp identified set, and the complete-erasure threshold q ≥ max ⁡ ( A , 1 − A ) q\geq\max(A,1-A) (Section 4 ). (2) Audit inversion. We give the threshold q ∗ q^{\ast} at which cross-component signal overtakes own-failure separability and show that the aggregate audit’s population maximizer is the full-outcome predictor, not the component oracle (Proposition 2 ). (3) The refresh trap. A controlled semantic-language stress test and a prediction-registered ECG study separate label mismatch from support mismatch and connect refresh to downstream harm (Section 5 ). (4) Support-preserving repair. We give matching passive label-complexity bounds and a designed two-mixture audit whose error does not depend on the deployed policy’s saturation (Section 6 ). Downstream selection/training-interface results are deliberately kept as a boundary analysis in the appendix. 2 Mechanism-first evaluation We test the chain implied by Eq. 1 , not a collection of interchangeable benchmarks. Proposition 2 is exact, but its engine and GSM8K checks reuse published quantities and are post-hoc. The GoEmotions study is a post-hoc natural multi-label text stress test with a small bag-of-words verifier; the AG News experiment is a more constructed control with 24 deterministic robustness splits rather than independent replications. Together they establish that the mechanism is not specific to engineered numeric features, not that our refresh effect has been measured with an LLM-scale semantic verifier. Contemporary rubric-RL work independently shows criterion-level saturation and scalar aggregation at LLM scale ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ; Tyagi et al., 2026 ) ; we use that literature only to establish interface relevance, not as validation of our inversion or refresh claims. The ECG refresh study is CPU-only and uses one benchmark whose component is a deterministic resource constraint, two head classes and ten subject splits; we did not refresh an LLM-scale verifier, did not study online RL with a refreshed verifier, and our prediction that refresh repairs the monitor failed. Engine and GSM8K policies are Qwen2.5, the strongest training result is offline DPO with three seeds, and ECG training is informative in one family. The audit requires trusted component labels (proxy bins change the estimand); the engine oracle is simplified, and ECG is a signal-processing benchmark, not a clinical validation. 8 Related work Modern post-training makes the component/aggregate interface concrete. Rubric RL scores prompt-specific criteria separately and then aggregates them into scalar on-policy rewards ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ; Mahmoud et al., 2026 ) ; policy-aware rubric work further shows that criterion informativeness changes with the policy because many criteria become saturated or dead ( Tyagi et al., 2026 ) . Fresh policy interactions are also used to refine reward or preference models ( Sun et al., 2025 ; Bai et al., 2022 ) . Two adjacent loop failures are especially relevant: on-policy optimization against one verifier can remove behaviors needed for later objectives ( Wei et al., 2026 ) , and a verifier useful on one task can regress a learner after task shift ( Lin, 2026 ) . We instead study the audit interface : full-outcome AUC can stop identifying one component, prefer an entangled verifier, and induce a harmful refresh even when the component verifier was initially correct. The statistical ingredients are classical. ROC behavior depends on case mix ( Sadatsafavi et al., 2022 ) ; partial identification and trimming bounds describe incomplete observables ( Manski, 2003 ; Tamer, 2010 ; Horowitz and Manski, 1995 ) ; deliberately varying mixture weights is a linear special case of finite-mixture identification ( Henry et al., 2014 ) ; the within/cross split parallels xAUC ( Kallus and Zhou, 2019 ) ; and the population AUC maximizer is the classical optimal ranker ( Clémençon et al., 2008 ) . We do not claim these ingredients as new. The new consequence is their combination under policy-induced semantic failure mixtures: complete loss of component identification, a calculable verifier-ranking inversion, and an audit-driven maintenance failure. Appendix roadmap The appendix is intentionally evidence-first. Appendices A–AD contain the oracle definitions, core audit-collapse controls, identification proofs, transfer checks, preregistration material and the refresh/semantic experiments that support the main claim. Appendices AE–AF are optional boundary analyses of downstream selection and DPO interfaces; they are not needed for Propositions 1–3 or the refresh-trap conclusion. Bundled scripts and frozen summaries are indexed in the supplement README; appendix-only workspace paths are provenance labels and do not imply that the corresponding large artifacts are packaged. Appendix A The engine oracle The solver decodes a design vector to a multi-zone body, computes its mass by integration, evaluates printability (overhang, minimum ligament and wall, DfAM flags) and envelope fit, and returns feasible as their conjunction, in 7.9 7.9 ms; the 200 000 200\,000 -row reference sample took 72 72 s. Its thermochemistry is checked against NASA CEA through rocketcea , independent of the project’s own Cantera path: across 28 28 operating points the maximum error is 0.25 % 0.25\% on chamber temperature and 1.7 % 1.7\% on characteristic velocity. The flow solver is grid-convergent on the Sod problem ( L 1 L_{1} error 0.0079 → 0.0042 → 0.0024 0.0079\to 0.0042\to 0.0024 at 100 / 200 / 400 100/200/400 cells) and reproduces the oblique-shock relation to 1.2 ∘ 1.2^{\circ} . Those checks cover the flow path, which is sized from the requirement and not the generator’s to choose. The on-target criterion is two-sided because under a one-sided one 86.4 % 86.4\% of on-target draws in the reference sample satisfy it by being small rather than by meeting the budget.
